minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 16, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:00 p.m., on May
16, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 11, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Ury (present until 6:35 p.m. at which time he departed
  and was absent for the remainder of the meeting)

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  May 16, 2011
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Manager’s Report

21.  Pension Reform and Employee Compensation

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that it is not appropriate to move ahead with an increase
  in employee compensation before the City Council has addressed the budget.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution No. 11-31, Declaring the City’s Intention to Approve an Amendment to the
  Contract Between the Board of Administration, California Public Employees’ Retirement
  System and the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo; (2) introduce Ordinance No.
  11-289, Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract Between the City Council of the City
  of Mission Viejo and the Board of Administration of the California Public Employees’
  Retirement System; and (3) adopt Resolution No. 11-32, Modifying the Employer Paid
  Member Contributions to the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (Effective
  July 8, 2011.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution No. 11-33, Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary
  Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications, Effective January 7, 2012 and (2) adopt
  Resolution No. 11-34, Modifying the Employer Paid Member Contributions to the
  California Public Employees' Retirement System (Effective January 7, 2012.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  2  May 16, 2011
 At the hour of 6:35 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Ury departed the meeting due to a family obligation.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council will continue their review of the City
Manager and there was no reportable action this evening.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Timeless Melodies

  The City Council received the presentation from Larry Maurer.

Council Member Schlicht vacated the dais at 6:40 p.m. and returned at 6:42 p.m.

P2.  Proclaim the Week of May 29 through June 4, 2011, as Cancer Prevention Week

  Mayor Leckness presented the proclamation to Ilda Oropeza, Director of Community
  Mission.

P3.  Community of Character Award

  Mayor Leckness presented the Community of Character Award to Ethan Taylor.

P4.  Presentation to the City by the Child Abuse Prevention Center

  Mayor Leckness received a certificate of appreciation from Scott Trotter, Executive
  Director of the Child Abuse Prevention Center, for the City’s support of the “Families
  Helping Families” campaign.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Hayes, M.V.: discussed the importance of Memorial Day and all national holidays.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that the small groups of residents who want facility upgrades
should pay for them. He feels that the tennis court renovation should be removed from the City’s
plan and the dog park should be funded by the dog owners themselves.

Cathy Jasper, M.V.: expressed concern with ongoing construction at a home on La Paja Lane.
She asked the Council to change the City's policies and procedures for residential construction in
order to implement time limitations and size restrictions.

Kime Goodrum, M.V.: asked the City Council to take public comments for agenda items earlier
in the evening.

City Council Minutes  3  May 16, 2011
 Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed his appreciation for the Mission Viejo Sheriffs personnel. He also
communicated his disappointment that a Council Member left the dais during a resident's
presentation earlier in the evening.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 6, 11, 13, and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 2, 2011, as
  presented.

3.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Third Quarter of
  FY 2010-11

  Received and filed.

5.  Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency - Third
  Quarter of 2010-11

  Received and filed.

7.  Check Register dated April 29, 2011, in the amount of $1,544,755.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  4  May 16, 2011
 8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2011

  Received and filed.

9.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2011

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for March 2011

  Received and filed.

12.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Concrete
  Sidewalks, Curb & Gutter, Driveway Approaches, and Cross-Gutters

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period
  of July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $680,000.00; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to S. Parker Engineering, Inc for the period of July 1, 2011,
  through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $340,000.00 pending adoption of the
  2011-2013 budget by City Council.

14.  Annual Park and Facility Hardscape Construction Improvements

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period
  of July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $110,000.00; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011,
  through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $55,000.00 pending adoption of the
  2011-2013 budget by City Council.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

16.  Service Cost Recovery Study

  Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing at 7:15 p.m.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Kime Goodrum, M.V.: expressed opposition to the increase in recreation fees.

City Council Minutes  5  May 16, 2011
   Shripathi Kamath, M.V.: stated that the increase in recreation fees are very reasonable for
  the service the residents receive.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo residents have amenities that residents
  of other cities do not.

  At the hour of 7:26 p.m., Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  adopt Resolution 11-30 Establishing New Fees for the Norman P. Murray Community
  and Senior Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 11-XX Establishing New Fees for the recreation centers.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Leckness
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: Ury

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Third Quarter of 2010-11

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the property that has been re-amortized and the
  process for watching those assets so they don't become valueless.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein replied that
  staff looked at everything of significant value in the City's two replacement funds. In
  many cases staff was able to extend the life of assets and in other cases the useful life was
  not increased.

City Council Minutes  6  May 16, 2011
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

6.  Check Register dated April 22, 2011, in the amount of $1,152,988.36

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments to Gretchen Thompson Consulting
  and to Management Partners. She asked staff to report back to her via email with an
  explanation of those expenses.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

11.  Building Plan Check and Inspection Services - Charles Abbott Associates, Inc.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Council Member Reardon highlighted the fact that the City will be paying lower fees for
  these services and she thanked staff for negotiating new, lower rates.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve an agreement with Charles Abbott Associates, Inc. for Building Plan Check and
  Inspection Services for the period from July 1, 2011 to June 30, 2013.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

13.  Annual Routine Maintenance Program for Sidewalk Grinding

City Council Minutes  7  May 16, 2011
   Council Member Schlicht asked why the company, BPR, Inc., changed its name and she
  inquired about the disparity in the bids.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay indicated that he doesn’t know why BPR
  changed its name or why there is a disparity in the bid amounts.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  award contract for the subject services to BPR, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011 through
  June 30, 2013 in the amount of $100,000; and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order
  to BPR, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to
  exceed $50,000 pending adoption of the 2011-2013 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

15.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Removal and Replacement of Asphalt
  Pavement and Related Services

  Council Member Reardon asked Public Works Director Keith Rattay to explain the
  difference between this asphalt overlay as compared to the Public Works overlay
  projects.

  Mr. Rattay responded that this contract is for asphalt repairs that are outside of the Public
  Works seven-year slurry and overlay programs.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  award contract for the subject services to Hardy & Harper, Inc. for the period of July 1,
  2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $598,600.00; (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to Hardy & Harper, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011, through June 30,
  2012, in an amount not to exceed $299,300.00 pending adoption of the 2011-2013 budget
  by City Council; (3) award the secondary contract for the subject program to Ben’s
  Asphalt Inc. for the period of July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of
  $397,400.00; and (4) authorize issuance of a purchase order to Ben’s Asphalt Inc. for the
  period of July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $198,700.00
  pending approval of the 2011-2013 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  May 16, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  No report due to Council Member Ury’s absence.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness presented the report.

20.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s report

22.  Street Sweeping Contract Renewal

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg stated that the City is currently out to bid for the street
  sweeping contract. He placed this item on the agenda to allow Sunset Property Services
  an opportunity to explain their request for a contract extension.

  Debbie Kaye, Sunset Property Services: presented the reasons why Sunset would like to
  extend their current contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  continue with the RFP process and deny the request from Sunset Property Services for a
  contract extension.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  9  May 16, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

At the City Manager’s request, Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill provided the City
Council with a status update on the installation of the starting blocks at the Nadadores complex.
He stated that staff is confident that the starting blocks will be in place before the next big swim
meet.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the
report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley noted that Council Members and staff are wearing purple shirts in
support of the Mission Viejo Relay for Life which will be held on June 4 and 5 at Saddleback
College. She encouraged anyone who would like to join her team, Kelley’s Heroes, to seek
further information at www.mvrelay.org. She also highlighted the unique opportunity for
residents to participate in a cancer prevention study (CPS-3.) In order to enroll, residents must
visit the Relay for Life between 11:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. on June 4. Council Member Kelley
outlined her attendance at a recent meeting regarding the future Capistrano Valley High School
performing arts center. She reviewed the construction schedule and announced that the
performing arts center is scheduled to be complete in June 2013. She also discussed the Oso
Parkway intersection improvements and stated that she has been very pleased with the non-
disruptive construction. Council Member Kelley announced that she will be out of town for two
weeks, returning at the end of May however she will be available via cell phone and email.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at the Bravo Burgers grand opening and the
Mayor’s Prayer breakfast. She joked with Mayor Leckness about forgetting Mothers Day and
she stated that the prayer breakfast was a wonderful event all the way around. She discussed her
attendance, as an alternate, at a recent City Selection Committee meeting in Costa Mesa. She
also attended a League of California Cities meeting where she was nominated to fill a vacancy
on the League’s Administrative Services Policy Committee. Lastly, Council Member Reardon

City Council Minutes  10  May 16, 2011
 outlined her attendance at a recent Association of California Cities Orange County meeting
where she learned that the City of Mission is already doing the things that other cities are just
beginning to do to cut costs.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she too attended the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast and the
Capistrano High School performing arts center meeting. Building the theater will be a logistical
challenge with construction during the school year but she feels it will be well worth the
outcome. She also outlined her attendance at the Saddleback Valley Unified School District
meetings regarding proposed school closures and she asked staff to pay special attention to the
Mission Viejo schools and any deed restrictions that would put limits on those properties. Ms.
Schlicht stated that the Council rushed through a salary increase at the beginning of the meeting
and the Mayor did not allow full presentation of that subject. She feels that staff is slowly trying
to push for salaries that are 5% above the median and that policy is no longer feasible because of
the economic situation that we are in. She referred to two recent reports that indicate that public
employees are paid more than private sector employees and she announced that she will bring an
agenda item back for further discussion and consideration. Council Member Schlicht stated that
she believes in public disclosure, public consent and there is not any transparency right now. She
read aloud the salaries of several top administrators and expressed concern that the City’s web
site lists a different amount than the W2 forms do. Finally, she noted that she appreciates the
City of Mission Viejo employees and she thinks they work very hard but public sector salaries
are too high.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness discussed his attendance at an Elks Lodge awards ceremony for notable local
students and how much he enjoyed hosting the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast at the Mission Viejo
Country Club. He noted that he recently had the pleasure of attending the Mission Viejo
Christian Church and he was very impressed by the energy and enthusiasm of the pastor and the
congregation. Mayor Leckness also attended the employee recognition luncheon to honor those
who have reached 5, 10, 15 and 20 years of employment with the City of Mission Viejo. He and
Council Member Kelley attended the grand opening of Rockin B’s Burrito Bandito in
Kaleidoscope which was the brain child of the owner’s son. Lastly, Mayor Leckness outlined his
attendance at a demonstration of the energy process that takes place at the San Onofre Nuclear
Generating Station (SONGS). He described what he learned about nuclear energy and stated that
he looks forward to touring SONGS in the near future.

City Council Minutes  11  May 16, 2011
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:03 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 6, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 6, 2011

City Council Minutes  12  May 16, 2011
